from_speaker: Half of the US economy’s growth
came from building data centers for generative AI
our_interpretation: Read economic growth as real GDP growth, following the immediately preceding reference to Q2 2025.
The context mentions multipliers, so the growth assertion may include indirect effects as well as construction and equipment expenditure.
Read the revenue comparison as worldwide industry revenue, with smartwatch revenue explicitly referring to 2024.

The period envelope covers the two components: 2024 smartwatch revenue and Q2 2025 GDP growth. For the undated current generative-AI revenue statement, use the latest completed quarter, Q2 2025, while retaining the missing annual or cumulative basis as a gap.
‘A little more’ means a modest excess; the speaker provides no numerical tolerance.
criteria.support_condition: A transparent Q2 2025 attribution puts generative-AI data-center buildout near half of US real GDP growth, and comparable industry revenue records show generative AI modestly exceeding 2024 smartwatch revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A measurement covering the claimed activities and effects places the GDP contribution materially away from half, or a consistently defined revenue comparison clearly fails the modest-excess description.
